evidence: Verg. Aen. IX 641: macte novā virtūte, puer
Traupman 193: Macte virtūte estō!, good for you!
terms.comment: The final e of macte is short.
Said by Dad in Libellus V.
Dad over the pies in Libellus IV.

terms.gloss: you are the pride of your family

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Hor.
evidence: Hor. Ars 327–330: eu! rem poteris servāre tuam
terms.comment: Greek εὖ, “well!”: praise for a right answer, or, in comedy, mock praise. Stronger is euge!.

phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

phrases.english: praise for a finished result: Dad over the pies, in Horace’s words (Ars 428)

phrases.latin: Pater puerum Rōmānōrum illud «Macte virtūte!» docuerat; quod igitur Baba Bulgaricē dīcit, puer ipse sibi Latīnē.
phrases.english: Dad had taught the boy the Roman “Macte virtūte!”; so what Baba says in Bulgarian, the boy says to himself in Latin.

phrases.latin: sī dē quīncūnce remōta est ūncia, quid superat? … — triēns. — eu! rem poteris servāre tuam.
phrases.english: If a twelfth is taken from five twelfths, what is left? — A third. — Good! You’ll be able to look after your money.
